example.title: Waterfront crab-shack restaurant on pilings over the bay (Joe's Crab Shack, Newport Beach)

brief: A waterfront seafood restaurant built out on timber piles over the bay (opened in the 1970s as a harbourside restaurant, re-themed as a crab shack in the 2000s): a long single-storey shed of weathered grey board siding under a low gable of rusty corrugated metal, a huge red neon-style sign letter by letter along the fascia, painted shark and hand-lettered boards ('FREE CRAB TOMORROW'), a railed deck and entry ramp, lamp posts, palms. One photo. Piles carried 10 m below the bed (spec rule 4).
label: Solana Pier
